messages:
ops-bot: [ALERT] SLO burn-rate triggered for project=model-inference (incident=INF-20250314-7) — p99 latency SLO burn 420% (5m window). paging @devon. link: https://redwood/integrations/alerts/INF-20250314-7

devon: ack — I'm oncall. seeing a spike in p99 from eu-west-1 starting ~12:03 UTC. not seeing a corresponding error-rate increase in the app logs yet. CPU/GPU utilization looks normal.

sam: joining — looking at queue depth/latency histograms now. can you dump the tail distribution?

devon: pasted a quick query, grabbing 1m histograms: `sum(rate(request_duration_bucket{le=\"0.5,1,2,5,10\"}[1m])) by (le)` — looks like a tiny traffic spike with a handful of very long requests, likely a client with huge context.

priya: is this causing customer pages? do we have any 5xx errors or timeouts?

devon: no 5xx. gateway timeouts remain ~0. We get increased latency but success rate is 99.99.

morgan: if it's not customer-facing failures, we should avoid hard paging for short-lived burn spikes. we've had noisy pages for 5m blips before.

elena: Agreed. This is classic burn-alert noise: a single heavy call can blow up 5m burn. We should gate paging on either sustained multi-window burn or an indicator of customer impact.

sam: I propose: keep 5m burn alerts for visibility but change the paging rule to require either 1) 5m burn > 300% AND 1h burn > 120%, OR 2) any customer-facing error-rate > 0.1% in the same window, OR 3) sustained 10m burn > 200%.

priya: sounds reasonable. also add a clause: exclude traffic from known large-batch clients (we tag them) so single heavy evals don't page ops.

devon: +1. For the short-term I'm going to mute paging so we don't wake up the infra on a noisy blip. I'll leave the alert visible in the channel for context.

pagerduty: Incident INF-20250314-7 acknowledged by devon. Pager duty escalation paused by oncall.

ops-bot: action log: paging suppression activated by devon at 12:12 UTC; existing alert remains non-paging.

sam: while paging is suppressed, I'll push a draft of the new burn-rate rule to the alerting repo. snippet: ```yaml
- alert: SLO_Burn_MultiWindow
  expr: |
    (burn_5m > 3 and burn_1h > 1.2) or
    (burn_10m > 2) or
    (customer_error_rate > 0.001)
  for: 2m
  labels:
    severity: page
```

elena: couple of comments: 1) set `for: 2m` to avoid flapping 2) add tag `impact:customer-facing` when customer_error_rate clause triggers so routing can choose SRE/product oncall. 3) include runbook reference in annotation.

priya: also add a metric gating on `affected_customers > 0` where affected_customers is computed by our downstream service mapping — that prevents pages for internal batch jobs.

devon: agreed. Make sure the rule cross-checks `request_origin != internal-batch` tag.

sam: putting the draft PR up: https://github.com/redwood/alerts/pull/418 — includes test cases for simulated spikes and a synthetic client that used to cause noise.

ops-bot: PR merged to `staging-alerts` at 12:34 UTC. New rule deployed to staging.

morgan: can we also add a dashboard tile showing multi-window burn trends (5m/10m/1h/24h) and a small table of top offending client IDs for the last hour? that'll help triage without paging.

elena: I'll make a quick grafana panel: distribution (p50/p90/p99/p999), burn windows, top client ID table, request counts, and a simple heatmap for queue depth. adding `INF-20250314-7` to the panel as a tag.

priya: follow-up actions: create infra ticket to update paging policy docs + notify product owners about the gating change. Also add a note to oncall runbook about using the new dashboard for triage.

devon: creating JIRA: INF-2412 "Revise SLO burn paging policy + dashboards" and assigning to morgan.

morgan: got it, INF-2412 assigned to me. I'll schedule a follow-up to harden the `affected_customers` computation and add tests for internal-batch exclusion.

sam: quick note: I also found a minor bug where KV cache misses spike if a client sends >256 tokens in a single request; it's contributing to CPU overhead on a tiny subset. Filed INF-2413 for that.

elena: dashboard deployed to `oncall/grafana/redwood-slo-burn` and shared. link: https://grafana/redwood/d/abcdef/slo-burn-multiwin (short-lived token expires in 7d).

devon: wrapping up timeline: 12:03 UTC initial 5m burn >400% triggered paging. 12:10 UTC triage determined no customer errors and small client spike. 12:12 UTC paging suppressed. 12:34 UTC new rule merged to staging and promoted to prevent similar noisy pages. 12:45 UTC dashboards added. No customer impact observed.

priya: please add notes to postmortem template: explain why we changed paging criteria and include a short example of the multi-window rule.

devon: done. Also setting a recovery note: ops-bot will auto-close the thread if no paging events for 6 hours. Leaving manual follow-ups in JIRA.

morgan: I'll pick this up in the morning and finish the tests. Thanks team. :thumbsup:

devon: thanks everyone — closing thread. If anything new pops up, reopen or @devon.
